_doc: What each culture on the caravan road values, shames, does and thinks of the road's other cultures (#1590). Ids and names are macro-world/cultures.json's (not edited here: it stays layout only). Read through src/artificer/culture-lore.ts; see docs/culture-lore.md.

voice.text: Dry as a summer field. They count twice, say half, and forgive slowly.

values.text: Patience with the land: you plant, you wait, you count.
Counting everything twice.
Keeping the farm whole: the land goes to the eldest child.

taboos.text: Moving a fence in the night. Fences move in daylight, with everyone watching, or not at all.
Forgiving too quickly. A quick pardon means the wrong didn't matter.

greeting.text: A word about the weather and a look at your boots: the mud says where you've walked.

trade.text: Barley is the coin of the valley. Even the goblins in the quarry are paid in it.

mourning.text: No prayers: the old gods are dead and their names aren't said. The family walks the dead one's fields and names what they grew.
mourning.source: WORLD.md § The weight of the past

debt.text: A debt is paid at harvest, never before, and counted twice when it is.

ridgefolk.text: Our neighbours up the slope. They keep the hill fires, we keep the valley fields, and we share the ford.

waterstead.text: Saltmere writes every sale down. Honest, and slow.

mountainhold.text: The holds ask what you've made. We ask what you've grown. Same question, really.

wallborn.text: The Gate counts you, and you remember being counted.

caravan-folk.text: Every spring the caravan brings someone half-dead out of the Reach.

grovekin.text: Grovekin heal with words and willow bark, and never hurry.

harborfolk.text: Harbour folk salt everything and argue about all of it.

steppe-camp.text: Steppe folk own nothing they can't carry. You can't plant a field like that.

refuge-keepers.text: The refuge takes in anyone the road spits out. We send them our spare bread.

ironborne-encampment.text: The ironborne bring ore down off the passes. We don't need much iron; a good plough lasts.

bazaar-folk.text: There's a goblin band in the old quarry above the ford. Neighbours, and we don't ask where the tools came from.

sayings.text: That is how we lose land here: one fence at a time.
We only built where the river let us.
Count it twice.

voice.text: Gruff and generous, and impossible to rush. Advice first, warmth after.

values.text: Generosity: advice for anyone who asks, whether they wanted it or not.
Doing it right the first time. A crude tool is a promise you'll fix it later.
Shares for all: land is split among all the children, not handed to one.

taboos.text: Breaking your word. Ridgefolk are bound by honour.
Rushing someone at their work. You wait until they're done.

greeting.text: Come to the hearth first. Nobody talks business on a cold doorstep.

trade.text: Stone and timber are sold by the cartload, and a handshake by the fire seals it.

mourning.text: The dead one's hearth is banked and left to burn out on its own. Nobody relights it until morning.

debt.text: Debts are shared like land: a family owes together and pays together.

fieldborn.text: Valley folk count everything twice and forgive slowly. Good neighbours at the ford.

waterstead.text: Saltmere's book has a page for everyone. Even us.

mountainhold.text: The holds ask what you've made, not whose child you are. Some of us left a hold seat for a forge.

wallborn.text: The Gate takes a toll on everything that moves. Sell before you get there.

caravan-folk.text: The caravan comes up the valley every spring when the snow lets go. We keep a fire lit for it.

grovekin.text: Grovekin healers listen to a wound before they touch it. Let them.

harborfolk.text: Salt comes up from the mere and our smoked meat goes down. Both keep a winter.

steppe-camp.text: Steppe folk keep the road past the mere. Under the Accords, nobody argues.

refuge-keepers.text: The refuge at Saltmere takes in anyone. We send down blankets when we can.

ironborne-encampment.text: Iron doesn't come from these hills. The ironborne bring ore down off the passes.

bazaar-folk.text: Goblin traders never name a price first, so they always win the bargain.

actually.text: They do wait for you to name yours, but that's caution, not cheating.

sayings.text: Make it sound the first time.
These hills give stone and grudges.
Fire first, talk after.

voice.text: Patient and precise, delighted by a new question, and always checking the book.

values.text: The book: every winter the Reach gives back is written down.
Telling anyone who asks what the book says.
Listening to water. It answers those who are patient with it long enough.

taboos.text: Tearing a page out of the book. A mistake is crossed through, never removed.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What shapes them

taboos.text: Letting the sluices silt up. Neglected water shames the whole stead.

greeting.text: Your name, where you came from and the day go into the book before the tea.

trade.text: Every sale is written in the book, and nobody argues with the book.

mourning.text: The dead one's page is copied out fair, and their last winter is read aloud.

debt.text: A debt is a line in the book, crossed through when paid. Unpaid lines are read out at the Moot.

fieldborn.text: Hollowford's harvests are in our book back forty winters. They don't know we have them.

ridgefolk.text: Ridgefolk tell you what they know slowly, by the fire. We write it down faster.

mountainhold.text: The holds trust a carved rune over a written page. Both last, if they're kept.
mountainhold.source: WORLD.md § Who uses it and how › The Bergfolk

wallborn.text: The book has Kestrel Gate's iron price for every year since the wall was built.

caravan-folk.text: Every caravan is in the book: the day it came, and who came with it.

grovekin.text: Grovekin heal by speaking. We write down what they say, when they let us.

harborfolk.text: The harbour folk salt the fish and we write down how much. Between us, the mere is kept.

steppe-camp.text: The steppe folk keep their records in songs. We've copied some down. They sing them better.

refuge-keepers.text: The refuge writes nothing down, so we keep its book for it.

ironborne-encampment.text: The ironborne doubled the iron price to get rich.

actually.text: The price has doubled in forty winters. The book doesn't say why.

bazaar-folk.text: Goblins sell us what they find in the ruins, and we must tell anyone who asks. They've never forgiven us.

sayings.text: Nobody argues with the book.
Water listens, if you've been patient with it.
Very few ask.

voice.text: Severe, then suddenly kind. They teach the way the mountain does: slowly.

values.text: What you make is who you are. Make something that will outlast you.
Merit over birth: the clan's elders lead, and craft decides who rises.
Patience with stone: dry-stone walls that stand three hundred years without mortar.

taboos.text: Touching another smith's tools without leave.
Letting the forge go cold. It is the hold's second hearth.

greeting.text: In the hall you name your craft before your family.

trade.text: Tools leave the hold rune-marked: who made them, and how.

mourning.text: A master is buried with their own tools.

debt.text: A debt is cut into the hall's tally-stone and cut out when it's paid. The stone remembers.

fieldborn.text: Valley farmers. They feed the hold and we shoe their ploughs. A fair trade.
fieldborn.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › The Building Alliance

ridgefolk.text: Half hold-blood and half valley. Some of the best of them left a hold seat for a forge.

waterstead.text: The Saltmere book writes down everything and makes nothing. Still, it's honest.
waterstead.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › What shapes them

wallborn.text: The Gate's wall is good stonework. Ours is older.

caravan-folk.text: The caravan carries our work down to the lowlands, where they pay silly money for it.

grovekin.text: Below the ash line the grovekin's herb book serves you better; above it, the mountain's herbs are bitter and true.

harborfolk.text: Harbour salt keeps the hold's meat. We pay in tools.
harborfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › What they make

steppe-camp.text: The steppe folk build nothing that lasts. They choose not to, which is odd.
steppe-camp.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What shapes them

refuge-keepers.text: A refuge built in a ruin. Better a ruin kept than a ruin wasted.

ironborne-encampment.text: Smiths trained in the holds go down to the encampment. Sabine did, and she likes being asked why.

bazaar-folk.text: There are no goblins in the holds.
bazaar-folk.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › Relations

actually.text: Goblin salvage bands live in the empty upper levels of three old holds.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › Relations

sayings.text: A mountain teaches slowly and forgives nothing.
Stonework is patience with a hammer.
What you make is who you are.

voice.text: Formal and careful. Every word is weighed as if it had a toll.

values.text: Keeping the wall: the toll pays for the wall, and the wall pays for the peace.
Counting: wagons, heads and goods, and the kestrels too.
Letters and records. The Gate values reading.

taboos.text: Slipping past the count. Dodging it shames you, not the Gate.
Saying aloud what the wall was built against. We stopped saying; we didn't stop keeping the wall.

greeting.text: You will be counted: wagons, heads and goods. Don't take it personally.

trade.text: Everything that moves through the Gate pays a toll, and the toll is folded into every price inside.

mourning.text: The dead are counted one last time: their name is read from the gate roll at dusk.

debt.text: A debt to the Gate is written in the roll. You can pass, but you'll be counted again on the way back.

fieldborn.text: Hollowford folk come through rarely, and keep the stamped paper on the wall for years.

ridgefolk.text: Ridgefolk carts bring stone and timber. Easy to count, slow to unload.

waterstead.text: Saltmere's book and our roll agree on most things. We check.

mountainhold.text: The hold above the Gate keeps its own counsel, and its own count.

caravan-folk.text: The caravan pays its toll and is counted here, every spring.

grovekin.text: Grovekin come through with herbs we can't name. We count them anyway.

harborfolk.text: Salt comes up to the Gate by the cartload and goes back as coin, less the toll.

steppe-camp.text: Viddfolk heralds pass with sealed cylinders. We count the herald, never the message.

refuge-keepers.text: Refuges inside old ruins. We'd wall them properly, if they'd let us.

ironborne-encampment.text: Every hinge on the gate is ironborne work.

bazaar-folk.text: The Compact's people come with stamped tokens instead of papers. We let them; the winch needs a goblin more often than the wall admits.

sayings.text: Kestrel Gate keeps the road. The road keeps us.
The toll pays for the wall. The wall pays for the peace.
We count the kestrels too.

voice.text: Practical and tireless, fond of every wagon like a relative, and always counting the miles to the next inn.

values.text: Reaching an inn before dark: under an innkeeper's roof no one draws a blade.
Getting everyone through. Nobody is left on the road if a wagon can carry them.
The wagons: every one looked after like family.

taboos.text: Drawing a blade under an inn's roof. That law is older than any kingdom.
Hoarding water on the road. What's in the barrel is everyone's.

greeting.text: "Road's long," and you offer a drink from your waterskin before you ask anything.

trade.text: Prices are kept in songs: every road has a song, and every song has the prices in it.

mourning.text: At the next inn the dead one's name is said, and the innkeeper sets out one more cup.

debt.text: Caravan debts ride from spring to spring. Everyone knows who owes Hedda three barrels.

fieldborn.text: Hollowford is the only ford before the spring flood. We cross there or wait a month.

ridgefolk.text: Ridgefolk feed you and give you advice you didn't ask for. Take both.

waterstead.text: Saltmere's prices are honest. The book sees to it.

mountainhold.text: Hold-made tools sell for silly money in the lowlands. Pack them carefully.

wallborn.text: The Gate counts the wagons, then the people, then the wagons again in case one walked off.

grovekin.text: Most of what ails a traveller is food, drink or sleep, missing. Our herbwife says so.

harborfolk.text: Hedda is owed by half the valley, and she tells everyone.

steppe-camp.text: The Viddfolk keep the steppe road. Where they sing, the road is safe.

refuge-keepers.text: The refuge takes anyone the road spits out. We've left a few there to mend.

ironborne-encampment.text: The ironborne mend axles at the Gate. Dear, but sound.

bazaar-folk.text: A goblin tinker on the wagon is worth two spare wheels.

sayings.text: Under an innkeeper's roof no one draws a blade.
Every road has a song, and every song has the prices in it.
Most years someone is waiting. Some years no one is.

voice.text: Unhurried and exact; soft-spoken, very old, and quietly amused by everyone.

values.text: Listening before touching: a wound is heard before it's treated.
A healing word works only when it's true, so you never lie to the sick.
Healing that is spoken, not brewed.

taboos.text: Promising a patient they'll be well when you don't know it.
Cutting a living tree. The grove is shaped, never felled.

greeting.text: A grovekin greets you by looking at your hands: frost and work leave marks you don't feel yet.

trade.text: Herbs are given to the sick and sold to the well.

mourning.text: The dead are laid among the grove's roots, and the living speak their name to the oldest tree.

debt.text: A healing is never owed. Bringing food afterwards is the custom.

fieldborn.text: Valley folk work until they break, then come to us. We'd rather see them sooner.

ridgefolk.text: Ridgefolk are gruff to hide how kind they are. We don't mind.

waterstead.text: The steads write down every cure we tell them. Some even work written down.
waterstead.source: WORLD.md § Who uses Rasa › The Lövfolk

mountainhold.text: Hold folk call Rasa sentiment. Their best smiths use it anyway, and don't say so.
mountainhold.source: WORLD.md § Who uses Rasa › The Bergfolk

wallborn.text: The Gate counts our herbs. It can't tell one leaf from another.

caravan-folk.text: The spring wagon brings the half-frozen out of the Reach. Some of us came that way ourselves.

harborfolk.text: Harbour folk are loud and warm. Good company for a slow recovery.

steppe-camp.text: Steppe folk heal on the move. We'd make them sit.

refuge-keepers.text: Clean water first, everything else after. The refuge has it right.

ironborne-encampment.text: Forge burns and ash coughs come down from the encampment. We keep salve ready.

bazaar-folk.text: Goblin menders fix anything but a fever. That's ours.

sayings.text: A healing word works better when it is true.
You learn what you can carry, and you leave the rest.
Drink, eat, sleep.

voice.text: Loud, warm, and never quite finished with an argument.

values.text: Keeping: the water gives, and we salt it and keep it.
Remembering debts, and getting them paid.
Building on stilts over the water, ready for it to change its mind.

taboos.text: Smoking a ration badly. Done well it lasts the winter; done badly, a week, and everyone knows who did it.
Forgetting a promise made at the water's edge.

greeting.text: A harbour greeting is a line of song, and you answer with the next one.

trade.text: Salt fish, salt pork, salt everything.

mourning.text: The dead one's name is carved into the piling anchors, beside the tide marks.

debt.text: A debt is remembered out loud, to everyone, until it's paid.

fieldborn.text: Valley folk buy our salt and complain about the price. Every year.

ridgefolk.text: Ridgefolk trade smoked meat for salt and never haggle. Suspicious.

waterstead.text: The steads keep the book and the sweet wells; we keep the salt. The mere needs both.

mountainhold.text: The holds buy salt by the barrel and pay in tools. Good tools.
mountainhold.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › What they make

wallborn.text: Salt goes up to the Gate by the cartload and comes back as coin, less the toll. Always less the toll.

caravan-folk.text: The caravan master owes us three barrels from two springs ago.

grovekin.text: Grovekin healers are quiet. We make up for it.

steppe-camp.text: Steppe folk speak in verses and eat our fish. Fair trade.

refuge-keepers.text: The refuge says don't drink at the north end of the mere. They're right; we don't.

ironborne-encampment.text: Ironborne hooks hold a net better than any others.

bazaar-folk.text: Goblins pay in news, and the news is usually good. Never once a lie.

sayings.text: The mere gives and we keep.
Smoked well, it lasts the winter. Smoked badly, a week.
A debt floats. It always comes back to shore.

voice.text: Few words, sharp eyes, and no patience for hurry.

values.text: Patience. It gets you more than arrows.
Keeping the road: a route-claim is the oldest promise in Mistheim.
Travelling light: a camp goes up and comes down in under an hour.

taboos.text: Hurrying the hunt, or the talk.
Leaving a fire-circle unswept when the camp moves on.

greeting.text: You come to the camp fire and wait to be offered a place. Then you tell what you've seen on the road.

trade.text: News is traded first and goods after. A camp that likes your road may buy your hides.
trade.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What they make

mourning.text: The camp sings the dead one's road, every verse, then moves on.
mourning.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What shapes them

debt.text: Under the Accords the road keeps its debts.

fieldborn.text: Valley folk fence the land. We don't understand fences, but we go round them.

ridgefolk.text: Ridgefolk light their fires on the hills. From the steppe we see them and know the road is clear.

waterstead.text: Saltmere's wells are sweet. We water the herds there and write nothing down.

mountainhold.text: The holds dig down. We go along. Both of us find things.
mountainhold.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What shapes them

wallborn.text: The Gate's verse is the shortest in the song: wall, toll, count, through.

caravan-folk.text: The caravan keeps to our road, and we keep it safe for them.

grovekin.text: A grovekin healer taught our hunters which plants the deer eat.

harborfolk.text: The harbour folk dry fish on racks by the mere. We trade them hides.

refuge-keepers.text: Lost riders end up at the refuge. We go and fetch them.

ironborne-encampment.text: Our arrowheads are Gate iron. An iron point comes back out of the deer.

bazaar-folk.text: Goblin news travels on our road. We carry it and say nothing.
bazaar-folk.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › Relations

sayings.text: Patience gets you more than arrows.
Snow tells you everything. Mud lies.
We don't take sides. We take the road.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What they make

voice.text: Brisk and tireless. They've seen too much to be surprised.

values.text: Taking in anyone the road spits out. That's what a refuge is.
Clean water first. Everything else after.
Using what's left: a refuge is built inside an old ruin.

taboos.text: Turning anyone away from the door.
Asking newcomers where they came from before they've eaten.

greeting.text: Water first, before your name. Then a bed, then questions, if there are any.

trade.text: A refuge doesn't sell. Everyone who stays mends something; that's the rent.

mourning.text: The lamps are always kept low; for the dead they're put out for one night.

debt.text: Kindness on the road comes back to the refuge's table: a stranger who was fed is fed again.

fieldborn.text: Valley folk send bread when the winter's hard. They don't say so.

ridgefolk.text: Ridgefolk send blankets and advice. We keep the blankets.

waterstead.text: The stead's wells are clean. We send our sick there for water.

mountainhold.text: Hold folk rarely need us. When they do, they don't say so.

wallborn.text: The Gate counts people. We just feed them.

caravan-folk.text: Every spring the caravan leaves someone with us who needs rest before the hills.

grovekin.text: Grovekin heal slower than we'd like and better than we can.

harborfolk.text: The harbour folk are loud, and they always have spare fish.

steppe-camp.text: Steppe riders bring us the lost from the open grass.

ironborne-encampment.text: The ironborne mend our hinges for nothing. We don't ask why.

bazaar-folk.text: Goblins built half our walls out of what they found. Good walls.

sayings.text: Clean water first. Everything else after.
That's what a refuge is.
You'll eat with us tonight.

voice.text: Blunt and funny, and proud of every hinge they've hung.

values.text: Good iron sings when you strike it. Bad iron argues.
Work that never runs out: hinges, axles, arrowheads.
Doing it twice to be sure: quench twice when the ash is on the anvil.

taboos.text: Selling bad iron as good.
Building anything crooked. The encampment is laid out true.

greeting.text: A nod at the anvil. You don't shake a smith's hand mid-strike.

trade.text: The ironborne bring ore down off the passes, and the best of it goes to the Gate's smiths.

mourning.text: As the Steinfolk do, they add to what the dead one made: one last rivet in their last work.
mourning.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › What shapes them

debt.text: A debt is paid in iron by weight, never in promises.

fieldborn.text: Valley ploughs last too long. Bad for business.

ridgefolk.text: There's a ridge smith at Hollowford who's hold-trained, whatever he says. You can hear it in his edges.

waterstead.text: Saltmere's book says iron is dear. The passes are steep. Both true.

mountainhold.text: Many of us were hold-trained before we came down to the encampment.

wallborn.text: Every hinge on the gate is ours. When it squeaks, that's the gate counting.

caravan-folk.text: The caravan breaks axles, we mend them, and it breaks them again. Good customers.

grovekin.text: Grovekin salve is the only thing for a forge burn.

harborfolk.text: Harbour folk want hooks by the hundred. We make them by the thousand.

steppe-camp.text: Steppe hunters buy our arrowheads. An iron point comes back out of the deer.

refuge-keepers.text: We mend the refuge's hinges for nothing. Somebody should.

bazaar-folk.text: Goblins buy the ore we don't want and sell it on to people who can't tell the difference.

sayings.text: Good iron sings. Bad iron argues.
A smith here never runs out of work.
Quench twice, to be sure.

voice.text: Smiling and careful, and never the first to name a price.

values.text: Everything has a price. Some prices are friendship.
Fixing nearly anything with what other people throw away.
Building into what's already there: rooms inside ruins, floors on top of floors.

taboos.text: Selling the same map twice.
Throwing away something that could be mended.

greeting.text: A smile, a kind word about your boots, and a long wait for you to speak first.

trade.text: Never name the price first. Let the buyer do it.

mourning.text: The warren keeps the dead one's tools in use. A tool that works is a goblin remembered.

debt.text: A debt can be paid in news, and good news pays double.

fieldborn.text: Hollowford calls us neighbours and doesn't ask where the tools came from. The best kind of neighbour.

ridgefolk.text: Ridgefolk tools are sound. In the lowlands they pay silly money for them.

waterstead.text: Tell a Saltmere scholar anything and the whole valley knows by spring.

actually.text: They must tell anyone who asks, but very few ask.

mountainhold.text: The holds say we don't live in their upper halls. We do.
mountainhold.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › Relations

wallborn.text: The toll-keeper drinks. Arrive at dusk.

caravan-folk.text: Caravan folk sell before the wall if they're clever. Most aren't.

grovekin.text: Grovekin pay in salves, and the salves are worth more than coin.

harborfolk.text: Harbour folk pay fair and complain loudly. We like them.

steppe-camp.text: The steppe road carries our news, and the heralds take a share.
steppe-camp.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › Relations

refuge-keepers.text: The refuge walls are our work. They never asked where the stones came from.

ironborne-encampment.text: The ironborne keep the best ore. We sell the rest to people who can't tell the difference.

sayings.text: Everything has a price at the Gate. Some prices are friendship.
Big folk call the edge of things the margin. We call it home.
Never name your price first.
